mlp.extrapolation: Linear interpolation through batch 1/8/32; the 8-to-32 slope extends to batch 64.

limitations: The study inherits E60's fitted-service, synthetic-tenant, immediate-rejection, and single-replica limitations.
Pacing spreads each fixed burst uniformly; it is an ingress shaping control rather than an optimized token bucket or tenant-aware queue.
Original client arrivals remain simultaneous, so reported end-to-end TTFT includes intentional ingress delay.
The burst period is deterministic and preserves mean rate but does not model production autocorrelation, retry storms, or cancellation.
Only actual-only and batch-32 equal-share controllers are tested; the objective is burst shaping rather than a new reservation-weight sweep.
model: E60 fixed request bursts spread across a fraction of their natural inter-burst period while end-to-end latency remains anchored to the original client arrival.

validation.latency_accounting: Scheduling uses paced arrivals, but queue latency, TTFT, E2E, and throughput elapsed time use the original client arrivals. Server-only latency and ingress delay are reported separately.
